skill.name: reactome-database
skill.description: Query Reactome pathway data, run enrichment analysis, map genes to pathways, and inspect molecular interactions for systems biology research.
skill.summary: Analyze genes, proteins, pathways, and enrichment results with Reactome REST APIs and helper scripts.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Confirmed findings are limited to expected Reactome network access and controlled result-file writes. The high device-file alerts are false positives from Reactome documentation URLs, and the command-execution alerts are Markdown formatting matches. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External Reactome requests can transmit gene identifiers or expression data.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users before submission and avoid sending private clinical or unpublished data without consent.

remediation.issue: The helper script writes output to a filename derived from the input path.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit output argument and refuse to overwrite existing files unless the user confirms.

remediation.issue: Reactome requests do not set timeouts in the helper script examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add reasonable request timeouts and clear retry guidance for long-running API calls.

content.value_statement: Biology teams need fast access to curated pathway data without memorizing Reactome endpoints. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pathway queries, enrichment analysis, and result interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Query Reactome Content Service endpoints for database versions, pathway records, entities, and molecular participants.
Submit gene or protein lists to the Reactome Analysis Service for enrichment results.
Retrieve prior pathway analysis results with Reactome analysis tokens.
Generate Reactome Pathway Browser links for selected analysis results.
Use the included Python helper script for version, query, search, entities, and analyze commands.
Reference documented input formats for overrepresentation and expression analysis.
limitations: Requires network access to Reactome public services.
Does not provide local copies of the Reactome database.
Analysis tokens expire after seven days according to the skill documentation.
The optional reactome2py package is described as functional but not actively maintained.

use_cases.title: Find enriched pathways from a gene list
use_cases.description: Submit identifiers and review significant Reactome pathways with p-values, FDR values, and matched entity counts.

use_cases.title: Inspect pathway participants
use_cases.description: Retrieve proteins, complexes, and small molecules that participate in a selected Reactome pathway.

use_cases.title: Create reproducible pathway summaries
use_cases.description: Use documented API calls and helper commands to create consistent pathway reports for teams.

prompt_templates.title: Look up one pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome skill to summarize pathway R-HSA-69278. Include its name, species, type, and a short biological description.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a gene list
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome Analysis Service for these identifiers: TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC. Summarize the top enriched pathways and FDR values.

prompt_templates.title: Compare pathway entities
prompt_templates.prompt: For pathway R-HSA-69278, retrieve participating physical entities. Group the first results by entity type and explain their roles.

prompt_templates.title: Build a reproducible workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Reactome workflow for a differential expression file. Include input validation, analysis submission, token handling, result filtering, and reporting steps.

output_examples.output: A concise pathway summary with the Reactome stable identifier, species, pathway type, biological description, and related participants.

output_examples.input: Analyze TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, and MYC for pathway enrichment.
output: Top enriched pathways ranked by significance.
Matched entity counts and FDR values for each pathway.
A Reactome Pathway Browser link when an analysis token is available.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workflow for expression analysis in Reactome.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step analysis plan covering TSV formatting, submission, token retrieval, significance filtering, and result export.

best_practices: Confirm that gene identifiers use supported formats before submitting analysis requests.
Tell users when identifiers or expression values will be sent to Reactome services.
Store analysis tokens only when users need to retrieve results within seven days.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private clinical or unpublished expression data without user approval.
Do not treat Reactome enrichment results as proof of biological causality.
Do not overwrite input files when saving helper script output.

faq.question: What is Reactome used for in this skill?
faq.answer: Reactome is used to query curated biological pathways and run pathway enrichment analysis on identifiers.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflows call Reactome public REST APIs hosted at reactome.org.

faq.question: Can it analyze gene expression data?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents TSV expression input and submission through the Reactome Analysis Service.

faq.question: Does it install third-party packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents optional reactome2py installation, but the included helper script uses requests.

faq.question: What files are included?
faq.answer: The skill includes SKILL.md, a Reactome API reference, and a Python query helper script.

faq.question: Is user data sent outside the workspace?
faq.answer: Yes. Gene lists and expression data are sent to Reactome when users run analysis requests.
